text: Horizontal overloads offer little value when the opposition congests the spaces between the lines. And that is precisely what has happened here. Arsenal initially went for the textbook approach: keeping Eze wide while overloading the right flank to create a vertical overload and play through that side. Even the central players were positioned towards the right which explains why the majority of Arsenal's attacking play came down that flank. However Forest have dealt with this quite well engaging in consistent duels and effectively blocking Arsenal's players in that zone. The best way to dismantle Forest's structure would be to employ a 'Pull-Push' tactic: draw their entire defensive structure towards the ball before releasing a runner in behind. The objective is to manipulate their defensive shape exploit the space created and ultimately dismantle the structure. We saw glimpses of this in the 31st minute when Rice clipped a ball in behind for a runner (most likely Ben White). This could be a valuable tactical weapon for Arsenal in the second half. A stalemate so far but a few subtle tactical adjustments could make all the difference.
